public_rationale: On the plain reading, Marcus said that in February 2025 no one had built AGI or shown a working way to build it. OpenAI's CEO wrote on February 9, 2025 that systems that 'start to point to AGI' were only 'coming into view' (e1). So AGI had not been built. Altman also said the road ahead 'looks fairly clear' (e2), but that is an expectation, not a shown method. As context, an October 2025 report says AGI still had not been declared and that an expert panel would now rule on any claim (e3). The claim holds on the plain reading. It would not be checkable if 'figured out' meant someone's private confidence.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'figured out' as 'shown to work' rather than 'privately believed'.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No one, including Altman, has yet figured out how to get to AGI.

statement.excerpt: The truth is nobody, not Altman, and not anyone else, has yet figured out to get to AGI.
statement.document_title: Breaking: OpenAI's efforts at pure scaling have hit a wall.

from_speaker: nobody, not Altman, and not anyone else
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post (February 2025), no one had built a system widely accepted as AGI or shown a validated method for building one.
A private belief that one knows the way (as Altman claimed) does not count as having 'figured it out' unless it is shown to work.
Target period: February 2025, the time the claim describes ('has yet').
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that in February 2025 no AGI system existed and no validated method had been shown, ideally from the parties claiming to be closest to it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that by February 2025 a system widely accepted as AGI existed, or that a method to build one had been publicly shown and validated.
